record.paper_title: On some open problems of Radu
record.original_question: In the same generalized probabilistic contraction setting, let alpha, beta, and gamma be the control functions used in the condition F_{f(x),f(y)}(alpha(t)) >= beta(F_{x,y}(t)), with gamma(s)=max(alpha(s),1-beta(1-s)). When the triangular norm T governing the Menger-space structure is replaced by an arbitrary Archimedean triangular norm, what conditions on alpha, beta, and gamma are appropriate to obtain a fixed point result?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(S,\mathcal{F},T)$ be a Menger probabilistic metric space, where $S$ is a nonempty set, $\mathcal{F}:S\times S\to\Delta^+$ assigns to each pair $(x,y)$ a distribution function $F_{x,y}\in\Delta^+$ (with $\Delta^+$ the set of left-continuous nondecreasing functions $F:[0,\infty)\to[0,1]$ satisfying $F(0)=0$ and $\sup_{t\ge 0}F(t)=1$), and $T:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to[0,1]$ is a triangular norm, in such a way that the usual Menger axioms hold:
(i) $F_{x,y}=H_0$ if and only if $x=y$, where $H_0(t)=0$ for $t\le 0$ and $H_0(t)=1$ for $t>0$;
(ii) $F_{x,y}=F_{y,x}$;
(iii) $F_{x,z}(s+t)\ge T(F_{x,y}(s),F_{y,z}(t))$ for all $x,y,z\in S$ and $s,t\ge 0$.

Recall that a triangular norm $T$ is called Archimedean if it is continuous and satisfies $T(a,a)<a$ for every $a\in(0,1)$.

Let $\alpha,\beta:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be control functions, and define
$$\gamma(s)=\max\bigl(\alpha(s),\,1-\beta(1-s)\bigr).$$
A mapping $f:S\to S$ is called a generalized probabilistic $(\alpha,\beta)$-contraction if for all $x,y\in S$ and all $t>0$,
$$F_{f(x),f(y)}(\alpha(t))\ge \beta\bigl(F_{x,y}(t)\bigr).$$

Problem. Assume $T$ is an arbitrary Archimedean triangular norm. Determine appropriate conditions on the control functions $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$ that guarantee that every generalized probabilistic $(\alpha,\beta)$-contraction $f:S\to S$ on a complete Menger space $(S,\mathcal{F},T)$ admits a (unique) fixed point.
artifact.category_tag: probabilistic metric spaces and fixed points
artifact.status_search_result: Web search reveals a substantial literature extending probabilistic contraction principles in Menger spaces under various t-norm classes (Archimedean, H-type, Dombi, Aczél–Alsina, Sugeno–Weber families) with control functions, including works by Hadžić, Pap, Mihet, and Radu. However, no source was found that explicitly settles the precise question of identifying optimal conditions on the triple $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ ensuring a fixed point for an arbitrary Archimedean t-norm; the question appears to remain a topic of ongoing research, so its status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: A generalized contraction principle in Menger spaces using a control function
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized contraction principle in Menger PM-spaces via control functions (extends Hadžić–Pap–Radu type results).
status_evidence.claim: Research continues on contraction principles in Menger spaces using control functions, indicating the problem area remains active.

status_evidence.title: Nonlinear contraction theorems in probabilistic spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Nonlinear contraction theorems for various t-norm classes in probabilistic metric spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions to Archimedean and other t-norm families are actively studied, but no definitive resolution of the specific (α,β,γ) question is reported.

status_evidence.title: Extension of contractive maps in the Menger probabilistic metric space
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses extensions of probabilistic contraction maps with different t-norm assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates ongoing extensions but not a definitive resolution of the Archimedean-t-norm version of Radu's question.
